summary.intent: Investigate the last two nightly CI runs, which had web soak failures that passed on retry, find the root causes, and fix the test harness.
summary.outcome: 10-28 Web Shares failure traced to a POST /auth/login that never reached Cloudflare (runner/network stall, not the API). 10-27 failure traced to a settings.spec test making a real call to ipfs.example. Both fixes (api-timeout retry class in loginRetry.ts, ipfs.example route stub in settings.spec.ts) were committed on a branch. The incident comments and PR were approved but not yet shown as done, and the stub was not confirmed by a local e2e run.

repo: Soak harness has no Playwright trace retention (#2434), so network-level evidence of stalls is unavailable.
Staging API (Nest) writes no HTTP request log, and Caddy has no access log for api-staging. Only the accelerator site has one.
Staging API exposes Prometheus metrics (http_request_duration_seconds). A challenge count above the login count indicates a login that never reached the API.
Client HTTP seam uses control_ms = 10_000 via AbortSignal.timeout in packages/client/src/seams/http.ts. A timeout surfaces as 'api transport error: seam error: signal timed out'.
loginRetry.ts did not retry the 'signal timed out' error. Retries are safe because each retry gets a fresh challenge.
settings.spec.ts:28 used the real https://ipfs.example as the dual pin provider. This causes a real network POST with a 60 s placement_ms wait and made the test flaky.
Running pnpm i modifies tracked Husky hook files, which must be restored before committing.
The Cloudflare Free plan lacks client ASN and edge TTFB in httpRequestsAdaptiveGroups.

code.finding: Defines control_ms = 10_000 as the API control-call timeout via AbortSignal.timeout.
Added an api-timeout retry class for 'seam error: signal timed out', counted in the summary.
Test now stubs https://ipfs.example/** instead of making a real network call.

workflow: Check the infrastructure logs the user asks about before concluding on a cause. Skipping them first drew a user challenge.
Cloudflare GraphQL MCP (graphql.mcp.cloudflare.com) enabled edge-level analysis. Adding with -s user scope makes it available in all worktrees.
MCP servers added mid-session are not visible until the session restarts.
Cross-checking sub-agent claims against the code and trace before reporting was worthwhile.
Cloudflare analytics queries are rate limited and the data is retained only briefly, so query soon.

friction: Initial analysis wrongly blamed the API without checking staging or edge logs.
The first Cloudflare MCP setup used local scope and did not load until a restart.
The Cloudflare GraphQL API rate limit forced a 5-minute wait.
A shell quoting error occurred while downloading logs.
Staging has no request logging, so the cause had to be inferred from metrics and Cloudflare.
pnpm i dirtied the tracked Husky files.
tsc had pre-existing errors, so only the changed files could be checked.
open_items: Push the branch, open the harness PR, and post triage comments on #2536 and #2532, then close them (approved, not yet confirmed done).
Confirm the ipfs.example stub works, including for worker requests, via a local e2e run of settings.spec.
Enable Playwright trace retention in the soak (#2434) to capture browser network data.
Check /auth/challenge and /auth/login latency if the api-timeout recurs.
Restricting the Cloudflare MCP to user scope was recommended; confirm it was done.
